items.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: And Paul gets more than anybody, Paul Gonsalves.

ctx.x: [inaudible]. You know I’ve seen us play, you know, jazz festivals with the band and everything. And it’s like Duke’s band was always the last one to go on. You know, nine times out of ten. It’s a lot of hanging around, so you get kind of sluggish you know. And Paul gets more than anybody, Paul Gonsalves. So what happened was, and all the musicians were around and everything, and in the opening the band is kind of tired out now, you know. And the band would sound terrible to me, you know. Okay now the next night…
Tell us about your work so far with the Statesmen. Tell us what it means to be in such an elite group and what that means historically for this music.
